Specification: A specification of a multi-car elevator system, modeling person and elevator state, call dispatching, door operations, and movement. It defines safety, type, and temporal invariants ensuring people eventually reach their destination floors and that all calls are eventually serviced.
IfThenElse: IF f1 > f2 THEN f1 - f2 ELSE f2 - f1
IF \E e \in Elevator : /\ CanServiceCall[e, call] /\ ElevatorState[e].doorsOpen THEN ActiveElevatorCalls ELSE ActiveElevatorCalls \cup {call}
IF p \in gettingOn THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = e] ELSE PersonState[p]
IF p \in gettingOff THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = eState.floor, !.waiting = FALSE] ELSE PersonState[p]
IF eState.direction = "Up" THEN eState.floor + 1 ELSE eState.floor - 1
IF closest \in stationary THEN [ElevatorState EXCEPT ![closest] = [@ EXCEPT !.floor = c.floor, !.direction = c.direction]] ELSE ElevatorState
SetEnumeration: {p \in Person : /\ PersonState[p].location = f /\ PersonState[p].waiting /\ GetDirection[PersonState[p].location, PersonState[p].destination] = d}
{e \in Elevator : /\ ElevatorState[e].direction = c.direction /\ \/ ElevatorState[e].floor = c.floor \/ GetDirection[ElevatorState[e].floor, c.floor] = c.direction }
FunctionConstructor: [Person -> [location : Floor \cup Elevator, destination : Floor, waiting : BOOLEAN]]
[Elevator -> [floor : Floor, direction : ElevatorDirectionState, doorsOpen : BOOLEAN, buttonsPressed : SUBSET Floor]]
[p \in Person |-> IF p \in gettingOn THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = e] ELSE PersonState[p]]
[p \in Person |-> IF p \in gettingOff THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = eState.floor, !.waiting = FALSE] ELSE PersonState[p]]
RecordConstructor: [location : Floor \cup Elevator, destination : Floor, waiting : BOOLEAN]
[floor : Floor, direction : ElevatorDirectionState, doorsOpen : BOOLEAN, buttonsPressed : SUBSET Floor]
ChoiceExpr: CHOOSE e \in stationary \cup approaching : /\ \A e2 \in stationary \cup approaching : /\ GetDistance[ElevatorState[e].floor, c.floor] <= GetDistance[ElevatorState[e2].floor, c.floor]
LeadsToOp: c \in ActiveElevatorCalls ~> \E e \in Elevator : CanServiceCall[e, c]
FunctionConstructor_ByDomain: [p \in Person |-> IF p \in gettingOn THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = e] ELSE PersonState[p]]
[p \in Person |-> IF p \in gettingOff THEN [PersonState[p] EXCEPT !.location = eState.floor, !.waiting = FALSE] ELSE PersonState[p]]
FunctionConstructor_SetType: [Person -> [location : Floor \cup Elevator, destination : Floor, waiting : BOOLEAN]]
[Elevator -> [floor : Floor, direction : ElevatorDirectionState, doorsOpen : BOOLEAN, buttonsPressed : SUBSET Floor]]
DivisionNotes: Vars/Floor/Direction/ElevatorCall/ElevatorDirectionState/GetDistance/GetDirection are pure value definitions; they go in OperatorDefNames_ValueDef.
CanServiceCall and PeopleWaiting reference unprimed state variables but are not actions; classified as state predicates.
TypeInvariant/SafetyInvariant are state predicates; TemporalInvariant uses ~> (leads-to) and TemporalAssumptions/Spec use temporal subscripts, so they are temporal properties.
All ten action operators (PickNewDestination..DispatchElevator and Next) contain primed variables and go in ActionDefNames (excluded from the four operator partitions).

TemporalNesting is true: TemporalInvariant contains \A c : c \in ActiveElevatorCalls ~> \E e ... where ~> abbreviates [](P => <>Q), and Spec uses [][Next] alongside fairness, producing nested temporal modalities.
